title: Testing, sanitizers and undefined behaviour
objectives: Design boundary/reference/property tests whose checks survive release NDEBUG, keep unsafe operations out of rejection tests and distinguish observed pass from all-input proof.
Reproduce a scoped instrumented build and interpret compiler/test/sanitizer diagnostics without treating a clean run as absence of every memory, business or concurrency error.
Apply testing, sanitizers and undefined behaviour invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: A test is an executable claim about a declared contract, source revision, toolchain and input. Use examples for understandable behavior, boundary cases for branch/range transitions, an independently derived reference for answers and metamorphic properties for related inputs.

blocks.md: A test is an executable claim about a declared contract, source revision, toolchain and input. Use examples for understandable behavior, boundary cases for branch/range transitions, an independently derived reference for answers and metamorphic properties for related inputs. None alone proves every possible input is correct. A property can pass for the wrong implementation: returning 0 for all additions is commutative, so add independent value/identity checks. Mutation, error status and output formatting are observable parts of the contract, not optional afterthoughts.

C assert and C++ assert macros can be disabled when NDEBUG is defined at inclusion. Do not put necessary validation, state changes or the only acceptance-test failure check inside assert. static_assert checks compile-time predicates; it cannot inspect arbitrary runtime input. Here tests use explicit conditionals/nonzero returns so the checks stay active with -DNDEBUG. Invalid input tests must verify rejection WITHOUT first performing the very overflowing/dangling/out-of-range operation being rejected.

blocks.caption: Expected output: boundary checks passed, exit 0. maximum+1 is never evaluated: the helper compares 1 with maximum-maximum first. Negative inputs short-circuit before the guarded subtraction where relevant. Run normal and -DNDEBUG builds to confirm these explicit checks are still present; that does not establish every possible arithmetic input or an actual app runtime.

blocks.md: The next small grid checks symmetry and the inverse relation (add(a,b)-a==b) where the accepted sums and subtraction are bounded/safe. It is derived testing evidence, not a second independent addition algorithm. Compare wider cases to a genuinely independent arbitrary-precision reference, and separately verify rejection/zero semantics at the type boundaries. A test harness can have its own bug; inspect it and test that it actually fails on a controlled wrong RESULT implementation without injecting undefined behavior.

blocks.caption: Expected output: 10201 property cases passed, exit 0. The grid is 0..100 in both arguments and every correct sum is at most 200. A fake implementation returning 0 would fail the inverse relation as soon as b > 0. Passing this finite grid is not a proof for all long long values; the pre-operation range argument and separate max boundary tests address a different part of the reasoning.

blocks.md: For a compatible GCC installation, an instrumented local build can use `g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all lesson.cpp -o checked`, then `./checked`. Compile AND link with the driver flags so sanitizer runtimes are linked. Keep the normal strict-warning build too. Exact option support, diagnostic text and runtime availability depend on compiler/target/environment; a failed runtime setup is not a passed sanitizer check or automatically a learner-code bug. Record the actual flags, source hash, exit status, stdout/stderr and test input.

AddressSanitizer instruments classes of invalid memory access such as out-of-bounds and use-after-free; UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer instruments selected undefined operations such as some signed overflow, null/alignment and shift errors. Enabled groups differ by compiler/version; do not copy a Clang-only flag into GCC and claim equivalent coverage. A clean instrumented run covers executed instrumented paths, not unexecuted branches, all allocators/libraries, all concurrency errors, semantic units, source authenticity or profitability. Ordinary unsigned modular arithmetic can be defined yet wrong for the business contract.

When a real report appears, preserve compiler/version/mode, input, source/stack location and full first relevant diagnostic; distinguish runtime setup failures from a source violation. Reduce to the smallest reproducer without deleting the failing contract, trace ownership/range, fix the cause, then rerun the reproducer and regression/reference tests. Do not suppress sanitizer output, disable the failing check, rely on a later plausible output or claim a randomized memory-layout rerun disproved the original issue. This lesson does not execute an intentionally undefined program as a teaching demonstration.

Independent transfer: add safe subtraction/multiplication test boundaries without evaluating an overflowing expected result. Compare with Python unbounded integer arithmetic under a declared source interface. Run explicit tests with/without NDEBUG and, if available, compatible instrumented flags. Introduce a controlled defined wrong result such as always returning 0 and show the test harness exits nonzero, then restore correct source. Keep actual execution evidence separate from runtime validation.

Sources: [GCC instrumentation](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Instrumentation-Options.html), [assert/NDEBUG](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/error/assert.html), [Clang ASan scope](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/AddressSanitizer.html), and [Clang UBSan groups](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.html). Clang documentation supplies conceptual comparison, not a claim that Clang or its flags were executed locally.

guidedExercise.prompt: Why do strict warnings, reference tests, range proofs and sanitizers all remain useful after one clean run?
guidedExercise.solution: They cover different failure classes and scopes: static diagnostics, expected business/value behavior, mathematical preconditions and selected dynamic operations. A finite clean run misses unexecuted cases and semantic/provenance/concurrency conditions. Record exact evidence without treating tools as universal certification.

independentExercise.prompt: Write a small test case that deliberately breaks the contract boundary in "Testing, sanitizers and undefined behaviour" and verify how your implementation rejects or handles it.
hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: A release macro must not remove required validation/effects or the only test failure signal. (Necessary runtime validation must not depend on an optional macro.)
A rejection test must not trigger the forbidden operation before reaching the code under test. (Validate rejection without executing an undefined expected computation.)
There are 101 choices for each argument, so 101*101=10201 cases.

Ownership, Sanitizers and Contracts when building reliable cpp and cpp memory workflows — specifically to design boundary/reference/property tests whose checks survive release NDEBUG, keep unsafe operations out of rejection tests and distinguish observed pass from all-input proof.

summary: Tests need independent answers and active failure checks, not only a green output or an assert compiled away.
Sanitizers diagnose selected executed operations; preserve real diagnostics and toolchain scope, fix causes, and never promote a clean local run into universal or app-runtime safety.
Design boundary/reference/property tests whose checks survive release NDEBUG, keep unsafe operations out of rejection tests and distinguish observed pass from all-input proof.

quiz.prompt: Why use explicit failure returns in these acceptance tests instead of only assert?
options: Every assert runs even when NDEBUG is defined
Explicit returns make a later external transaction atomic
static_assert can inspect every runtime request
quiz.explanation: A release macro must not remove required validation/effects or the only test failure signal. (Necessary runtime validation must not depend on an optional macro.)

quiz.prompt: Why not compute maximum+1 to build the expected rejection value for signed long long?
options: The expected expression itself would overflow
The expected value should use unsigned wraparound and be treated as the signed sum
A later cast repairs all earlier undefined operations
Only production arithmetic can have undefined behavior
quiz.explanation: A rejection test must not trigger the forbidden operation before reaching the code under test. (Validate rejection without executing an undefined expected computation.)

quiz.prompt: How many ordered input pairs lie in 0..100 for both a and b?
quiz.explanation: There are 101 choices for each argument, so 101*101=10201 cases.

quiz.prompt: A clean instrumented run establishes what?
options: All conceivable paths and dependencies are certified
Financial units and authentication are proven
No concurrency error can exist anywhere
No enabled diagnostic fired on the recorded executed paths
quiz.explanation: Clean local instrumentation is useful bounded evidence, not a universal proof. (Record compiler/source/flags/input and remaining limits.)

quiz.prompt: An instrumented binary cannot initialize its runtime in the current environment. What should the report say?
options: The learner implementation passed memory safety under standard assumptions
The sanitizer check is unavailable/failed setup, not passed
All ordinary tests must be deleted
Suppress stderr and count the exit as success
quiz.explanation: Distinguish unavailable instrumentation from a source violation and from a successful run. (Investigate environment and retain ordinary test evidence separately.)
